disposition_reason: Narrative 'systematic' review (keywords + 6 databases, no PRISMA, no pooling) that tabulates honey metal means from cited studies (Table 1) and makes apiary-siting and container/storage statements; no new honey measurements, so no occurrence findings are extracted here, only control/mitigation statements.
disposition_locator: Method for review, printed p.239; Results/Table 1, printed pp.240-241; Discussion, printed pp.241-242; Conclusion, printed p.243

study.design: review (narrative; described by authors as systematic review; keyword search of Google Scholar, SID, Scopus, PubMed, Science Direct, ISI; no PRISMA, no inclusion criteria, no pooling)
study.material_scope: honey (literature); bee bodies and pollen mentioned only as context
study.growing_origin_vs_market: not applicable (secondary); Table 1 rows labelled by country only, origin vs purchase market not distinguished
study.method: not applicable (review); cited studies used ICP-OES, ICP-MS, ICP-AES, AAS, FAAS, GFAAS, HGAAS and others per Table 1 'Method' column
study.basis: Table 1 units heterogeneous and unharmonised (ug/kg, ppm, mg/kg, ug/l, ppb, ug/g, ng/g, mg/L, 'mg/kg d.w', 'mg/kg wet weight')

controls.control: Locate honey-production hives away from highways and railways
controls.comparator: Croatian/Kosovo honey Pb vs other European countries' reported values
controls.outcome: Authors state Croatian and Kosovo findings of honey Pb higher than other European countries 'highlight the need' for hive siting far from highways and railways.
controls.locator: printed journal page 241 (PDF p.5), Discussion, right column; text copy lines 369-381
controls.note: Guidance is the review authors' inference; the cited studies' design (whether road distance was measured) is not described in the review.

controls.control: Avoid apiaries near industrial centres / industrial areas
controls.outcome: Review reports a direct relationship between honey metal contamination and industry-related environmental pollution / number of industrial centres; industrial-city honey higher than rural honey (Nigeria).
controls.locator: printed journal page 241 (PDF p.5), Discussion, left and right columns; continued p.242 top; text copy lines 376-399
cited_primary: Al-Khalifa & Al-Arify 1999 (cited for a Turkey study; the reference is a Saudi honey physicochemical/pollen paper)
Samimi et al. 2001 (Saveh, Markazi, Iran: Cd and As)
controls.note: Statement 'amounts of heavy metals ... (especially cadmium and mercury) were higher than permissible rate' is attached to the Al-Khalifa & Al-Arify 1999 citation; citation-content match is doubtful (see unresolved).

controls.control: Air and surface-water pollution near apiary as metal source
controls.outcome: Positive relationship between honey metal content, respiration of contaminated airborne particles and contaminated surface water.
controls.locator: printed journal page 241 (PDF p.5), Discussion, left column; text copy lines 399-408

controls.control: Volcanic soils / volcanic activity as a geogenic source
controls.outcome: Volcanic activity affects honey (Etna); high honey Al in Chile (6.15 +/- 4.53 mg/kg) attributed to colonies on volcanic soils; Cd 0.01-0.05 mg/kg.
controls.locator: printed journal page 241 (PDF p.5), Discussion, left column; text copy lines 409-427
controls.note: Values are the review's restatement of a cited study; not extracted as occurrence.

controls.control: Separate environmental-origin from beekeeping-origin contamination sources
controls.outcome: Honey contamination sources classified into environmental origin and those related to beekeeping and maintenance; another source is contact with contaminants, tools, beekeeping practices, floral sources, utensils, insects, animals and water.
controls.locator: printed journal page 241 (PDF p.5), Discussion, left column; text copy lines 354-364; printed journal page 242 (PDF p.6), Discussion, left column; text copy lines 449-455
cited_primary: Mahmoudi et al. 2014 (reference title is an oxytetracycline-residue ELISA/HPLC paper)
controls.note: Cited reference does not obviously support a metals statement; treat as review-author assertion.

controls.control: Use coated / solderless storage cans; avoid bare metal containers for acidic honey
controls.outcome: Honey (average pH 3.9) can corrode metal cans over time; suitable coatings and solderless cans can reduce Pb and Sn in honey.
controls.locator: printed journal page 242 (PDF p.6), Discussion, left column; text copy lines 457-471
cited_primary: Bonyadian et al. 2011 (reference title: 'Determination of lead, tin, copper and cadmium in Iranian canned fish')
controls.note: Cited reference is a canned-fish study, so the honey-specific claim is not directly supported by its citation.

controls.control: Storage of honey in metal containers / wax composition raises Pb
controls.outcome: Waxed honey contained more lead than other samples, attributed to storage in metal containers and wax chemical composition.
controls.locator: printed journal page 242 (PDF p.6), Discussion, left column; text copy lines 471-479
cited_primary: Bonyadian et al. 2011 (canned-fish reference; see note)
controls.note: Same citation mismatch as above; no numbers given.

controls.control: Bee filtering: honey carries less metal than bees and pollen
controls.outcome: Adult bee bodies reported more contaminated than pollen and honey; bees appear to reduce contamination while producing honey; honey metals significantly lower than in bees due to filtering by bees.
controls.locator: printed journal page 242 (PDF p.6), Discussion, left col. bottom and right col. top; text copy lines 481-485, 398-404; printed journal page 243 (PDF p.7), Conclusion; text copy lines 505-509

controls.control: Honey (and bees) as bioindicator of environmental metal pollution
controls.outcome: Honey is used as an indicator for measuring environmental pollution such as heavy metal pollution.
controls.locator: printed journal page 239 (PDF p.3), Introduction, right column; text copy lines 169-171

controls.outcome: Authors conclude that studying the quality of honey in the consumer market is necessary to protect consumers, and the public should be informed.
controls.locator: printed journal page 243 (PDF p.7), Conclusion; text copy lines 509-516; abstract p.237 lines 44-46

controls.outcome: Lists ICP-OES, FES, FAAS, ICP-MS, HPLC, AAS, TXRF, GFAAS, HGAAS; ICP-OES described as most applied, with excellent sensitivity.
controls.locator: printed journal page 242 (PDF p.6), Discussion, right column; text copy lines 454-485

controls.control: Compare honey results with national/FAO-WHO limits and PTDI
controls.outcome: Cites ISIRI (Iran) PTDI for Pb, Cd, Hg, As (0.0036, 0.001, 0.007, 0.0021 mg/kg bw); several cited studies report honey below FAO/WHO or Indian limits; Toma et al. report Fe/Cu/Mn/Zn above WHO/FAO 'maximum allowable concentration'.
controls.locator: printed journal page 241 (PDF p.5), Discussion, left column; text copy lines 364-376; printed journal page 242 (PDF p.6), Discussion; text copy lines 439-448, 430-436
controls.note: PTDI units printed as 'milligrams per kilogram of temporary bodyweight' (sic); no honey-specific ML is stated in the review.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Summary gives Italy (Quinto 2016) Cr as '116 +/- 10.7 ug/kg'; Table 1 prints '12.8+/-10.7' in the Chrome column (PDF p.4, text line 259).

Summary assigns Sobhanardakani & Kianpour 2016 '56.15 +/- 54.32 ug/kg' to Al; in Table 1 the value starts at the Nickle column (character offset 113, header 'Nickle' at 113; Aluminium at 124), i.e. Ni not Al.
Summary assigns Ghana (Magna 2018) '15.785 +/- 10.968 mg/kg' to Al; the value sits in the Nickle column (same offset analysis, text line 254), i.e. Ni not Al.

Summary states Akbari/Saghaei market Pb as '0.011, 0.935, and 0.04 mg/kg'; Discussion prints '0/11, 0/935, and 0/04 mg/kg' (= 0.11) and Table 1 Akbari Lead is 0.11 +/- 0.05 mg/kg (p.242 lines 406-416; p.240 line 226).

Summary describes Aghamirlou 2015 as 'Markazi Province, n=25 industrial-area samples ... attributed to industrial proximity'; Table 1 gives no region or industrial attribution for that row; the Saveh/Markazi industrial statement in the Discussion is attributed to Samimi et al. 2001 and concerns Cd and As.
Summary frames 'Turkey/Iran: Cd and Hg above permitted limits'; the source attaches that statement to a Turkey study cited as Al-Khalifa & Al-Arify 1999, not to Iran.
Summary attributes the bee-body > honey filtering observation to Altekin 2015 / Piven 2020; the source attributes it to Samimi et al. 2001 and Bogdanov 2006.

Summary says Table 1 aggregates '28 cited studies across 19 countries, sampling years 2010-2021'; Table 1 has 29 rows from 18 country labels (incl. 'Tadla-Azilal', Morocco), its title says 2011-2021, the Year column runs 2010-2020 and contains a typo '1017' (Ghana) and '2019' for Bilandzic et al. 2011.

Summary describes Bhalchandra & Baviskar findings and Hungary MP-AES discrepancy correctly; Croatia Al 288.5 and Fe 82.5 'mg/kg' reported in summary without noting the unit is implausible for honey (likely ug/kg or a transcription issue in the review).
unresolved: Header citation gives pages 238-248 but printed page numbers run 237-246; locators here use printed page numbers.

Several citations do not match the claims they support: Bonyadian et al. 2011 (canned fish) for honey container/storage Pb-Sn; Mahmoudi et al. 2014 (oxytetracycline residues) for beekeeping-practice contamination sources; Al-Khalifa & Al-Arify 1999 (Saudi honey physicochemistry) for a Turkish industrial-centres finding; Tuzen et al. 2007 (Turkish honeys) for a 'study done in China'; Saghaei et al. 2012 (Iran) for a 'study conducted in Saudi Arabia'. Control statements resting on these citations should be traced to an actual primary before use.
Table 1 column alignment in the pdftotext layout is ambiguous for some sparse rows; column assignments above were checked by character offset only for the rows named in contradictions.
Units in Table 1 are not harmonised and some appear implausible (Ghana Pb 79.815 mg/kg; Croatia Al 288.5 mg/kg); review values must not be used as occurrence data.
